key_insight: A U-Net predicts full 36-component 3D strain localization tensor fields, with width and depth emerging as the key architecture scaling parameters.
engineering_relevance: The surrogate could accelerate repeated mechanical-field evaluations in concrete homogenization and coupled multiscale simulations.
method: Train on voxelized concrete mesostructures up to 256³ using localization tensors from an FFT-based linear elastic solver.
Optimize U-Net hyperparameters to identify architecture scaling rules and accuracy–speed trade-offs.
Use Maximum Mean Discrepancy on internal feature maps to flag out-of-distribution microstructures without reference solves.
evidence_signal: The final model achieved 1.118% Mean Absolute Error on both validation and held-out test sets and approximately 8.7× faster inference than the FFT solver on an Nvidia H100 GPU.
watch_item: Generalization depends on training morphology diversity; transfer across aggregate volume fractions does not establish reliability for arbitrary microstructures.
paper_title: Neural network scaling and generalization for 3D strain fields in heterogeneous materials
